answer_1.quote: We build a model upon Longformer-Encoder-Decoder (LED), where the encoder predicts the preference score (Ranking), aspect ratings and confidences (Rating) while the decoder generates the comments (Reasoning).
answer_1.outputs: preference score, aspect ratings, confidence scores, explanatory comments

answer_2.quote: Existing methods which use referenced metrics (e.g., BLEU , METEOR , ROUGE ) and unreferenced metrics (e.g., UNION , ) deviate from human preference.

answer_3.quote: Following Ghazarian et al. ( ), we use Longformer-Encoder-Decoder (LED) to produce a preference score, as well as ratings and comments for the pre-defined aspects.

answer_4.quote: We collect human judgments for the stories in WP (sampled from test data...), where each story is assigned to 8 annotators. Annotators are asked to rate each story on a scale of 1 to 5 (from poor to good).
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rate each story on a 1–5 scale and provide brief reasons for their rating; they also compare paired stories before rating.
criteria: coherence (when distinguishing human vs. machine stories)
